title: Deleting functions
recap: A deleted function participates in overload resolution but cannot be called. Deleting a better-matching overload prevents a call from silently converting to another overload.
This is an interface property, not a text-matching exercise. The tests ask the compiler whether a particular call is well formed instead of searching for a particular source line.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement wholeUnits(int units): return units when nonnegative, otherwise 0. Also prohibit calls with a double by declaring the double overload deleted. Add that declaration in the indicated API area, not an implementation that truncates. The visible compile-time tests verify that int calls are valid and double calls are not.
expectedOutput: wholeUnits(2.5) must not be a valid call
hints: The extra declaration has the same name and a double parameter.
Use = delete rather than a function body.
A deleted exact-match overload blocks conversion to the int overload.
